sections.heading: C — Traffic signs: colors, shapes and regulatory signs
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signs: colors, shapes and regulatory signs

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A20
Traffic signs speak through symbols and words, and a driver should recognize each one fast from its shape, its color and the words, numbers or symbols printed on it. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A20
The main background color of a sign is a quick clue to the kind of information the sign carries. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A20
A red sign tells you to stop, to yield, not to enter, or that you are going the wrong way. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A20
A yellow sign gives a general warning about what lies ahead. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A20
White is used for speed limit signs, keep right signs and some guide signs. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A20
An orange sign warns of a construction or maintenance work area. [A20]
Why it matters: orange is the work-zone color, not yellow.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A20
A green sign shows destinations, distances and directions. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A20
A blue sign points to services such as food, gas and rest areas. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A20
A brown sign marks recreation areas and places of cultural interest. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A20
Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school, pedestrian and bicycle signs. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A20
Fluorescent pink is used for signs at emergency traffic incidents. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A20
Black is the color of One Way signs and of signs whose messages change. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A20
An octagon, the 8-sided shape, always means stop, and you must bring the vehicle to a complete stop. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A20
A triangle means yield: slow down and stop if you need to so that other vehicles and pedestrians get the right-of-way. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A20
A diamond-shaped sign warns of special conditions or hazards ahead, so be ready to slow down and react. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A20
A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no passing zone begins, and you must not pass other vehicles there. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A20
Rectangles are regulatory or guide signs: a vertical one usually states an instruction or rule of the road, while a horizontal one usually gives directions or information. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A20
A pentagon, the 5-sided shape, warns of a school zone and marks a school crossing. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A20
A round sign gives warning that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A20
A crossbuck sign stands at a highway-rail grade crossing to show exactly where the railroad crossing is. [A20]
Why it matters: the round sign warns of a crossing ahead; the crossbuck marks the crossing itself.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A20
A trapezoid sign marks recreation and cultural interest areas and National Forest Routes. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A21
Regulatory signs state traffic laws, and you are required to obey them. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A21
The stop sign, white letters on red, is the only 8-sided sign you will meet on the road. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A21
At a stop sign, stop completely at the stop line; with no stop line, stop before the crosswalk; with neither, stop before you enter the intersection. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A21
After stopping at a stop sign, yield to the vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection and stay stopped until you can safely enter and go through. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A21
The yield sign, red letters on white, is the only sign with its 3-sided shape. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A21
Approaching a yield sign, slow down, look left and right, and yield to pedestrians, bicycles and vehicles, then go on only when it is safe. [A21]
Why it matters: a yield sign does not always require a stop, but it never lets you go before the way is clear.
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A21
Rectangular 4-sided signs with black lettering on white regulate traffic, and the speed limit sign among them gives the maximum speed for the stretch of road where it stands. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A21
Regulatory examples in the manual include signs that ban right turns, left turns, U-turns or all turns, plus Left Turn Only, Do Not Enter, Wrong Way, No Parking, No Turn on Red and Do Not Pass. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A21
Further regulatory examples tell you to keep right of a median, to yield on a green light when turning left, that a lane is a bike lane, or that parking is reserved for disability permit holders. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A21
A Two-way Left sign means drivers coming from either direction may use the center lane to make a left turn. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A21
A One Way sign means traffic may move only in the direction its arrow points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A21
A High Occupancy Vehicle lane may be used only when your vehicle carries the number of people marked on its sign. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

Glossary: regulatory sign — a sign stating a traffic law you must obey [A21]. Warning sign — a sign alerting you to a condition or hazard ahead [A20]. Crossbuck — the sign that marks the spot of a highway-rail grade crossing [A20]. Pennant — the sign shape marking the start of a no passing zone [A20]. High Occupancy Vehicle lane — a lane limited to vehicles carrying the posted number of people [A21].
Memory aid: count the sides — eight sides means stop, three means yield, five means school [A20].
Misconception: orange and yellow are not interchangeable; yellow is a general warning while orange means a construction or maintenance work area [A20].

items.skill: sign recognition by shape and color (octagon, triangle, diamond, pennant, pentagon, round, crossbuck, trapezoid)
items.why: each meaning is tied to a visual shape or background color, so learners need picture-based recognition drills rather than text-only cards
